articles.title: GardenBench: A lightweight, daily evaluation of LLM capabilities
articles.summary: We introduce GardenBench, a benchmark with 11 test suites that evaluate the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across a range of tasks.
articles.paragraph: We introduce GardenBench, a benchmark with 11 test suites that evaluate the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across a range of tasks. By systematically prompting LLMs with various lightweight queries, we document day-to-day changes in model performance, including run costs and times, that other benchmarks miss. This allows us to compare the accuracy and features of responses across model providers and versions. We account for daily variations in model accuracy, capturing both model progress and degradation, for instance, when a model is changed post-deployment or when a new model is released. We base our evaluation on general-use tasks and make our results publicly accessible via a live dashboard, diversifying existing approaches to LLM testing.

articles.title: Doing Less with More: A First-Principles Exploration of the Suitability of Agentic Computing over Alternative Architectural Choices
articles.summary: There is growing interest in automating business activities with Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) due to latter's seeming ease of use. Never has it been easier, or costlier, to do less with more.
articles.paragraph: There is growing interest in automating business activities with Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) due to latter's seeming ease of use. Never has it been easier, or costlier, to do less with more. However, little is known about when agents are preferable to established alternatives such as local computation, Representational State Transfer (REST), the Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP), and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), particularly when development speed, performance, and operational cost are considered. We investigate this question using a controlled mathematical task that compares seven methods on a benchmark of 1,000 arithmetic expressions where semantics of operator precedence has to be preserved.

articles.title: What Social Media Teaches Us About Accumulative AI Risks
articles.summary: Prominent AI safety discussions emphasize existential threats and catastrophic events, such as AI-enabled nuclear conflict or engineered biological outbreaks.
articles.paragraph: Prominent AI safety discussions emphasize existential threats and catastrophic events, such as AI-enabled nuclear conflict or engineered biological outbreaks. This position paper argues that there is another type of AI risk that arises and accumulates from the widespread use of AI. Drawing on lessons from social media, we argue that safety assessments must also address accumulative harms that develop through repeated use, recurring decisions, and feedback across interconnected deployments. Repeated reassurance, selective exposure, recurring decision biases, and growing personal profiles may gradually narrow perspectives, weaken independent judgment, or enable exploitative influence without a single clearly harmful event.

articles.title: LogicVal:A Logic-Formalized Benchmark for Constraint Satisfaction in Text-to-Image Generation
articles.summary: Text-to-Image (T2I) generative models have made significant progress in producing high-fidelity images from natural-language prompts.
articles.paragraph: Text-to-Image (T2I) generative models have made significant progress in producing high-fidelity images from natural-language prompts. Alongside this progress, numerous benchmarks have been developed to evaluate capabilities such as attribute binding, numeracy, spatial reasoning, and commonsense reasoning. In this work, we propose a new perspective on T2I evaluation by casting it as a constraint-satisfaction problem. We introduce a logical framework that formally specifies the benchmark domain, including objects, attributes, and relations, alongside the constraints that generated images must satisfy.

articles.title: European Innovation Council backs 43 projects to turn breakthrough research into prototypes
articles.summary: The selected projects bring together 218 organisations from 30 countries, including 24 EU Member States.
articles.paragraph: The selected projects bring together 218 organisations from 30 countries, including 24 EU Member States. The European Innovation Council (EIC) has selected 43 groundbreaking projects under the EIC Pathfinder Open 2026 call, each of them receiving up to €4 million in grant funding. From pioneering cancer treatments and quantum computing to advanced manufacturing and climate-resilient technologies, these projects aim to push the boundaries of scientific discovery and lay the foundations for tomorrow's breakthrough innovations. The 2026 call received for the second consecutive year a record number of proposals, making the Pathfinder open call one of the Horizon Europe most competitive calls and showing the relevance of bottom-up funding.

articles.title: Depth-dependent soil water-salt relationships in the Hetao Irrigation District, arid Northwest China: Implications for sustainable management
articles.summary: by Yuanqing Cao, Huihui Wang, Xuan Chen, Li Zhu Soil salinization threatens agricultural productivity in arid gravity irrigation systems worldwide, yet the depth-stratified relationships between soil...
articles.paragraph: by Yuanqing Cao, Huihui Wang, Xuan Chen, Li Zhu Soil salinization threatens agricultural productivity in arid gravity irrigation systems worldwide, yet the depth-stratified relationships between soil water and salt content remain poorly characterized. We monitored soil moisture and electrical conductivity (EC) at six depths (0–100 cm) across 15 sites in the Hetao Irrigation District, China, during the 2025 growing season. Our results indicate a depth-dependent divergence in water–salt associations. The EC-derived salinity index varied from 0.08 to 42.91 g/kg, exhibiting extreme spatial heterogeneity (coefficient of variation (CV) = 185.2%) across the salinity gradient. However, moisture-salinity relationships showed marked depth dependency.

articles.title: Integrating machine learning and geospatial technologies for spatio-temporal analysis of urban expansion and land use transformation in Gambella Town, Ethiopia
articles.summary: by Kanenus Fufa Dararo, Goanar Jal Dup, Weyesa Merga Chemeda, Shankar Karuppannan Rapid urbanization and the associated expansion of built-up areas are transforming land resources, ecosystem functions...
articles.paragraph: by Kanenus Fufa Dararo, Goanar Jal Dup, Weyesa Merga Chemeda, Shankar Karuppannan Rapid urbanization and the associated expansion of built-up areas are transforming land resources, ecosystem functions, and the spatial structure of cities. Distinguishing urban growth, urban expansion, and urban sprawl is essential for understanding the processes and patterns of urban transformation and supporting sustainable urban planning. This study integrates machine learning and geospatial technologies to analyze spatio-temporal land use and land cover (LULC) dynamics and urban expansion in Gambella Town, Ethiopia.

articles.title: Bitcoin Optech Newsletter #427
articles.summary: This week’s newsletter summarizes the disclosure of two denial-of-service vulnerabilities in older versions of Eclair and describes a proposed scheme for running complex multi-round contracts inside L...
articles.paragraph: ● Disclosure of two DoS vulnerabilities fixed in Eclair v0.14.1: Erick Cestari posted to Delving Bitcoin the responsible disclosure of two denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerabilities in the channel opening process of Eclair v0.14.0 and earlier. Both were fixed in Eclair #3324 and released in v0.14.1 in July, and users running an older version should upgrade. The first, found by Matt Morehouse with his smite fuzzer, is a race condition in a duplicate temporary_channel_id check. Eclair checked whether the ID was already in use before accepting an open_channel message, but did not record the new channel until a later step, so an attacker sending several identical open_channel messages in quick succession could get two past the check.
